correctness.rationale: For symmetric n-vertex weights in [0,1] with w_ii=1 and initial opinion diameter below the confidence radius, the all-interacting FOAF system is w_ij’=(w_ij+(W²)_ij/n)(1-w_ij). The polynomial vector field preserves the weight cube, symmetry, and initial component block zeros and is analytic. For every missing within-component pair at initial distance d>=2, the first nonzero Taylor term has order d-1 and coefficient S_ij/n^(d-1), where S_ij sums products over all shortest paths. The inductive coefficient recursion uses d(i,k)+d(k,j)>=d and exactly d-1 interior split vertices on each shortest route, explaining the cancellation of the derivative factorial. Since S>0, every such tie becomes positive for all positive times; logistic comparison yields saturation to one inside components, while cross-component ties stay identically zero. Strict monotonicity of missing within-component ties yields one crossing of each epsilon in (0,1), with the stated small-epsilon inversion. The result is explicitly restricted to the persistent all-interacting regime; no claims made for changing confidence switches.

originality.rationale: The continuous FOAF vector field and qualitative triadic closure are established by Nugent–Gomes–Wolfram; support confinement to initial connected components is also discussed there. The exact analytic order d-1, weighted geodesic coefficient S_ij/n^(d-1), all-positive-time component closure and sharp epsilon first-crossing time are additional mathematical consequences not identified in inspected original sections. Stochastic binary-edge triadic closure models have different generators, so their density/bistability conclusions do not imply these analytic Taylor coefficients.
